newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Police tighten security in Sri Lankan capital.
newsitem.headline: Police tighten security in Sri Lankan capital.

text.p: Sri Lankan police tightened security in the capital Colombo on Thursday ahead of the anniversary of last year's Central Bank bombing and Independence Day celebrations next week, police said.
Scores of plainclothesmen had been mobilised and additional checkpoints set up to search vehicles entering the city, they said.
"We have intensified security in the city, deployed a special police team and are appealing to the public to be extra vigilant," Colombo police chief D.M. Dissanayake told Reuters.

He said the precautions were based on information about suspected activity by the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), who are fighting for independence in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
He said tightened security would also serve Independence Day celebrations on February 4, when top government officials and foreign diplomats were expected to attend a ceremony.
The police announcement comes a day before the first anniversary of the devastating Central Bank bomb attack by a suspected LTTE suicide bomber.
The January 31 bombing killed 100 people, wounded about 1,400 and destroyed part of Colombo's prime commercial area.

Security guards at Colombo's main bus terminal have also been placed on high alert after police on Wednesday discovered 25 grams (less than one ounce) of an explosive material, a detonator and some ammunition in a bus.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is higher.
